title: Halloumi and Roasted Pepper Salad
subtitle: Charred halloumi with sweet roasted peppers and mint
excerpt: Roasting the peppers brings out their sweetness. The halloumi is fried in a hot pan until deeply golden and served immediately while the outside is still crisp. This is a good weeknight main or a generous starter.
sourceNotes: Halloumi originates from Cyprus and has been produced on the island for centuries. Its high melting point makes it one of the few cheeses that can be grilled or fried without losing shape.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the peppers up to a day ahead. Fry the halloumi and assemble just before serving.

content.text: Pat the halloumi slices dry before frying. Surface moisture causes spitting and prevents browning.

items.prepNote: deseeded and cut into wide strips
deseeded and cut into wide strips

content.text: Toss the pepper strips with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Spread in a roasting tin in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until soft and charred at the edges.
Pat the halloumi slices dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over a high heat.
Fry the halloumi for 2 minutes each side until deeply golden. Do not move it while it browns.
Arrange the spinach on a large plate. Top with the roasted peppers.
Lay the halloumi over the peppers. Squeeze over the lemon juice.
Scatter over the mint leaves. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Pan was not hot enough before adding the cheese.
items.fix: Wait until the oil shimmers before adding the halloumi.

items.cause: Moved too early before a crust formed.
items.fix: Leave it untouched for 2 full minutes before attempting to flip.

items.symptom: Peppers are soft but not sweet.
items.cause: Oven not hot enough or peppers overlapping in the tin.
items.fix: Use a large tin so peppers are in one layer. Roast at full heat.
